faqs.q: Why are roof rats such a problem in St. Augustine?
faqs.a: Roof rats are Florida's main structure rat, and St. Augustine gives them exactly what they want: palm crowns, fruit trees, dense shrubs, and rooflines they can reach from fences and branches. They nest in attics and wall voids and breed year-round here. Our crew traps and excludes — sealing the entry and cutting back roof access — and frames structure work as nonchemical trapping and exclusion, because chemical rodent work in a structure is FDACS Chapter 482 pest-control territory.

St. Augustine.wildlife_intro:
In St. Augustine, our crew's steady calls are raccoons in attics and chimneys, eastern gray squirrels at soffits and gable vents, and roof rats moving from palms and fruit trees onto rooflines. Opossums and striped skunks work yards after dark, armadillos dig lawns and beds, eastern moles tunnel the sandy ground, and Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats roost in older rooflines through the warm months. The county's habitat — historic St. Augustine, beach communities, and fast-growing northern suburbs — and features such as Matanzas River, Guana Tolomato Matanzas Reserve, Anastasia State Park, St. Johns River western edge keep that pressure close to housing in every season.

Florida has no winter shutdown for this work, so St. Augustine jobs run year-round, with the one hard legal gate being bats: exclusion is legal only from August 15 through April 15, and maternity-season bat calls become inspection and scheduling. Our crew works under FWC Rule 68A-9.010 with the property owner's authorization — Florida issues no nuisance-trapper license — checks any live trap at least every 24 hours, and seals the entry as part of the job so the next animal cannot use the same opening. Call us at (844) 544-3498 and tell us what you are hearing or seeing.

faqs.q: We found small mice near our St. Augustine Beach dunes — can you trap them?
faqs.a: No, and we will explain at your door: the Anastasia Island beach mouse is a federally Endangered subspecies that lives only in these dunes, and harming or trapping one is a federal violation. Beach mice are nocturnal, pale, and dune-bound — they do not infest houses. Mice inside a home, away from the dunes, are house mice and legitimate work, confirmed by location and sign. If your mice are in the dunes, the correct action is admiration from a distance and a call to the state park or FWC if you see disturbance.

faqs.q: Alligators are part of Sawgrass life — when does one become FWC's problem?
faqs.a: At four feet plus a threat. The lakes at TPC and across Ponte Vedra hold resident gators that residents and golfers coexist with daily; FWC's nuisance program acts when an alligator is four feet or longer and poses a danger to people, pets, or property, and only its contracted trappers may remove one. Keep the dawn-and-dusk bank discipline with dogs, never feed, and report bold behavior. An alligator sunning on the far bank is the community working as designed — and it is also why our raccoon work here never involves the waterline at night.

faqs.q: Rats are around our Hastings packing shed — what is the fix?
faqs.a: Containment and closure. Packing sheds draw rats with spilled produce and harborage in stacked materials; we trap the population with nonchemical methods, seal the shed's entries with gnaw-proof flashing, and set the discipline — waste produce contained daily, pallets pulled from walls, vegetation cut back. Chemical programs belong to Chapter 482 licensees. A Hastings shed run this way starves its own rat problem within a season, because the fields offer the survivors easier living than a sealed building.

faqs.q: Squirrels nest in our Fruit Cove attic every winter — how do we break the cycle?

Gray squirrels here den in attics for the winter litter and return to known sites yearly; a summer inspection finds the entries while the attic is empty, metal-backed sealing closes them, and trimming oak limbs back from the roof removes the commute. Winter trapping alone removes this year's tenants and advertises the vacancy to next year's. Our Fruit Cove quotes price the summer seal as the main event, because in canopy suburbs it is.
